## What it is

LibreChat is a web chat for AI models with agents, MCP tools, file uploads, presets and conversation history. It talks to local models (Ollama) and to hosted providers ([LibreChat-AI/LibreChat](https://github.com/LibreChat-AI/LibreChat)). The Market description is written from the GitHub description without its list of provider names.

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API; license-matrix row "LibreChat"). Market class **L1**. Upstream marks every GitHub release as a pre-release; v0.8.8 is the newest without an `-rc` suffix.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): ai: chat, agents. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with three containers: `api` (LibreChat), and native sidecars `ferretdb` and `postgres`.
- **Database (deviation from upstream):** upstream runs MongoDB, whose server licence (SSPL-1.0) is not one the Market can ship. This package uses FerretDB 2.7 (Apache-2.0), which speaks the MongoDB protocol, on FerretDB's `postgres-documentdb` image (PostgreSQL with the DocumentDB extension). LibreChat keeps FerretDB compatibility tests in `packages/data-schemas/misc/ferretdb/`, but they "are NOT run in CI": UNVERIFIED until the OneMind smoke test passes and a real conversation has been saved and reloaded.
- Both sidecars listen on 127.0.0.1 only, so PostgreSQL trusts local connections and FerretDB authentication is off; there is no database password and no Secret.
- `CREDS_KEY`, `CREDS_IV`, `JWT_SECRET` and `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET` are generated by LibreChat itself on the first start and kept in `/app/data/.env.temp` (mode 0600) on the data volume, as upstream's compose file does (`LIBRECHAT_TEMP_CREDENTIALS_PATH`).
- `librechat.yaml` (ConfigMap) adds one endpoint: the Ollama Market app at `http://ollama.app-ollama.svc.cluster.local:11434/v1/`, as the LibreChat docs page "Ollama" configures it.
- All containers run non-root: LibreChat and FerretDB as UID 1000, PostgreSQL as UID 999. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volumes: `librechat-data` (10 GiB: `data/`, `uploads/`, `images/`) and `librechat-db` (5 GiB). Probes: `GET /health`.

## First run

Source: [librechat.ai/docs](https://www.librechat.ai/docs) and the docs page "Ollama".

1. Install Ollama and pull a model (see its README), then install LibreChat and approve the action. It installs into `app-librechat`.
2. Create your account. Sign-up is off (`ALLOW_REGISTRATION: "false"`, also upstream's behaviour when unset), so nobody who reaches the page first can claim it. Accounts are made with upstream's `create-user` script (`config/create-user.js`), which asks for the password or generates one when left blank. The first account becomes the administrator:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-librechat exec -it deploy/librechat -c api -- npm run create-user -- <email> "<name>" <username>
   ```
   Repeat for each household member.
3. Forward the port, open http://localhost:3080 and sign in:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-librechat port-forward svc/librechat 3080:3080
   ```
4. Pick "Ollama" as the endpoint and a pulled model.

## Not done yet

- Meilisearch (message search), the RAG API and the admin panel are not packaged.
- Hosted providers need their keys in `librechat.yaml` or the environment; none is configured.
- Scheduled chats are off: without Redis the log says "scheduler NOT started" at every start. This pod is one process, the case `.env.example` describes for `SCHEDULES_SINGLE_PROCESS=true`; turning them on is a later, deliberate choice.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: it has not been tested against this image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices where upstream gives none; they are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212765046, job `gate (librechat)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `registry.librechat.ai/librechat-ai/librechat:v0.8.8`: GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7 in `dompurify` 3.4.16 (fixed 3.4.17); CVE-2026-106445 and CVE-2026-106446 in `handlebars` 4.7.9 (fixed 4.7.10); CVE-2026-125120 in `mongoose` 8.24.1 (fixed 8.24.3); CVE-2026-90711 in `proxy-addr` 2.0.7 (fixed 2.0.8); CVE-2026-59873 in `tar` 7.5.13 (fixed 7.5.19).
- Vulnerability: `ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0`: CVE-2026-33815 and CVE-2026-33816 in `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` v5.7.6 (fixed 5.9.0); CVE-2026-33186 in `google.golang.org/grpc` v1.75.0 (fixed 1.79.3); CVE-2025-68121 in Go `stdlib` v1.25.4.
- Vulnerability: `ghcr.io/ferretdb/postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0` (Debian 12 base): CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-42496 and CVE-2026-8376 in perl (`perl`, `perl-base`, `perl-modules-5.36`, `libperl5.36`); CVE-2026-33845 and CVE-2026-42010 in `libgnutls30`; CVE-2026-44172 and CVE-2026-49261 in `libmariadb3` and `mariadb-common`; CVE-2026-2781 in `libnss3`; CVE-2026-31789 in `openssl`, `libssl3` and `libssl-dev`; CVE-2026-23112, CVE-2026-43037 and CVE-2026-98432 in `linux-libc-dev`; CVE-2026-111497 in `libbrotli1`; CVE-2025-68121 in Go `stdlib` v1.24.6. Each has a fixed version in the Debian archive.
- Secret finding (Trivy): `jwt-token` (MEDIUM) in `/app/packages/data-schemas/src/config/parsers.spec.ts` of the librechat image (a test fixture).
- Licence: no row for LibreChat in `research-output/evidence/license-matrix.csv`, so the app is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10). GitHub reports MIT, which matches the manifest. The app still carries `UNVERIFIED` markers (README, deployment.yaml), which also cap the tier at community.
- Passed: ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.

**Hold (apps/market-unblock-2, 2026-11-13):** 5 npm CVEs in the app image, Go and Debian CVEs in `ferretdb` and `postgres-documentdb` (both at their newest tags), a test-fixture JWT, and no licence-matrix row. The LibreChat registry (`registry.librechat.ai`) is not reachable from the worker, so newer app tags could not be read. Unblock: fixed upstream images and a licence-matrix row (a research file, outside `apps/`).
